summary.brief: Joanne prepares, cooks, and serves crispy orange chicken with rice.
summary.detailed: The video opens with Joanne introducing her orange chicken recipe, then she cuts a pound of chicken breast into bite‑size cubes, zestes an orange and squeezes the juice, which she combines in a skillet with soy sauce, honey, rice wine, sesame oil, grated ginger and cornstarch, whisking and heating until the mixture bubbles and thickens into a glossy orange glaze. In a separate bowl she whiskes two eggs, folds in corn starch and a splash of soy sauce to make a batter, coats the chicken pieces in the batter and tosses them. She heats vegetable oil to about 365 °F, adds the battered chicken in small batches using tongs, and fries the pieces for a few minutes until they turn golden and are fully cooked, then lifts them with a spider and drains on paper towels. The fried chicken is returned to the skillet and tossed in the orange glaze until evenly coated, after which it is plated over a bed of white rice, sprinkled with sliced scallions and a few strips of orange zest. Joanne tastes the dish, shows her enjoyment, and then eats a bite with chopsticks, dipping the chicken into the rice and adding extra orange peel; the segment ends with her speaking to the camera and a montage of thumbnail images promoting her other Chinese‑takeout‑at‑home recipes.

action.detailed: Coat the chicken cubes in batter, fry them until golden, then toss them in the orange glaze and serve over rice.

summary.brief: Joanne makes orange chicken by cutting the meat, creating an orange glaze, deep‑frying the pieces, and serving them over rice.
summary.detailed: Joanne introduces the orange chicken recipe, then, wearing a yellow‑and‑white striped shirt and a white latex glove, she cuts a pound of chicken breast into bite‑size cubes on a cutting board. She zestes an orange with a micro‑zester, halves it and squeezes out about a half‑cup of juice, which she pours into a skillet, strains out any seeds, and adds soy sauce, honey, rice cooking wine, sesame oil, the orange zest, grated ginger and a little corn starch, whisking everything together and cooking until the mixture bubbles and thickens into a glaze. In a separate bowl she whiskes two large eggs, adds a quarter‑cup of corn starch and a tablespoon of soy sauce, creating a pale, frothy batter. She tosses the chicken cubes in the batter, heats vegetable oil to roughly 365 °F, and uses tongs to fry the pieces in small batches until they turn golden, crispy, and are fully cooked, draining them on paper‑towel‑lined plates. The fried chicken is transferred to the orange glaze, tossed to coat evenly, then placed on a bed of white rice, sprinkled with sliced scallions, and finally she tastes a piece and comments on the balanced sweet‑savory flavor before presenting the finished dish.

action.detailed: Cut the chicken into bite‑size cubes, zest and juice an orange, whisk the glaze ingredients together and heat until thick, whisk eggs with corn starch and soy sauce to form a batter, coat the chicken pieces, deep‑fry them until golden and crispy, toss the fried chicken in the orange glaze, and serve over rice topped with scallions.
